name: Dependency Pairs and Estimated Dependency Graphs
description: Extracts finite KO7 call graphs and proves termination by well-founded dependency pairs. TCAP estimation over-approximates the real graph and internal replay inherits well-foundedness.

program.name: The Termination Axis
program.summary: The rule recΔ b s (δ n) → app s (recΔ b s n) copies its payload and consumes one counter; a direct measure orients it exactly when it ignores the payload and increases strictly with the counter, and the additive, affine, matrix, arctic, tropical and Knuth-Bendix families fail under their stated premises, with mutual cycles and higher-order sharing as variants. The proofs that succeed change the observer: the dependency-pair projection to the counter, nonlinear coupling, and the lexicographic and multiset path orders; seventy-six methods and a residual catalog record the verdicts as bookkeeping.

oneLine: Every KO7 dependency pair strictly decreases a counter-depth rank so the reverse pair relation is well-founded, and every real DP edge is covered by its TCAP estimate.
summary: Objects are KO7 traces with the single dependency pair DPPair from recDelta b s (delta n) to recDelta b s n, the ranks dpRank and counterHeight, finite call graphs with SCC search, first-order and TPDB extractions, TCAP estimates with real and estimated edges, and an internal record of the TTT2/CeTA certificate replay. The questions are pair extraction from the eight KO7 root rules, orientation of all pairs and SCC paths by a rank, refutation of global orientation from finite SCC data, and coverage of real edges by estimated edges. Every DPPair step strictly decreases dpRank and the reverse relation DPPairRev is well-founded; the replay record stores projection index 3 and pair count 1 as recorded constants, and its projection problem is the same internal KO7 problem, so it adds no proof independent of the internal descent. Extraction is sound and complete with only R_rec_succ extracting a pair, the other seven rules are pair-free, and a spurious control pair is neither a Step nor a DPPair. Finite rule carriers, head views and array-backed extractions yield eight-node KO7 call graphs with a recDelta self-loop; TCAP over-approximates real edges for every first-order system, with the KO7 self-loop covered and a negative estimated edge absent; and the linear measure counterHeight orients the pair problem, so a blanket barrier against natural-number orientations of the pair problem is false. The pair relation is deterministic and confluent, normalization takes at most dpRank steps, and bounded reachability agrees with reflexive-transitive closure on finite graphs.
boundary: By definition a measure orients the dependency-pair relation if it strictly drops along every pair, and then it drops along every SCC path by transitivity; an SCC pair with m source ≤ m target refutes orientation. On KO7 only R_rec_succ extracts a pair, the single pair decreases the counter rank dpRank and the linear counterHeight, and the reverse pair relation is well founded, so no barrier holds for natural-number orientations of the pair problem. TCAP estimation over-approximates real edges for every first-order system, so an absent estimated edge certifies an absent real edge; the replay record of the external certificate reuses the internal pair problem and records its indices.

conclusions.statement: The reverse KO7 dependency-pair relation DPPairRev is well-founded, with no extra hypotheses.
For all traces a and b, if DPPair a b then dpRank b < dpRank a.

The replay record of the external TTT2/CeTA certificate records projection index 3 and pair count 1 as constants, and its projection problem is the internal KO7 problem, so its pair relation is DPPair and its reverse relation is well founded by the internal proof.
For all traces a and b with DPPair a b one has dpRank b < dpRank a, and ko7FastReplay.projectionProblem.Pair = DPPair with WellFounded ko7FastReplay.projectionProblem.Rev, and WellFounded DPPairRev.
For every TRS and pairs s and t, every real DP edge is an estimated TCAP edge.
If there is no estimated edge from s to t then there is no real edge from s to t.
For all schema nodes a and b, every KO7 real edge yields a KO7 estimated edge.
For every Step h from a to b, existence of c with DPPair a c holds if and only if extractsDP h holds.
For all traces a and b, given h : Step a b and hex : extractsDP h, there exists c with DPPair a c.
For all traces a and b, if DPPair a b then counterHeight b < counterHeight a.
There exists μ : Trace → Nat such that for all traces a and b, if DPPair a b then μ b < μ a.
It is false that for all μ : Trace → Nat, if for all traces a and b with DPPair a b one has μ b < μ a then False.
There is no estimated edge from the negative source pair to the negative target pair.
For all traces a, b and c, if DPPair a b and DPPair a c then b = c.
For all nodes a and b, Reachable R a b holds if and only if ReflTransGen R a b holds.

openPoints: Pair-level extraction and source soundness for rule-record frontends need additional structure beyond the constructed call-head records.

Finite-carrier, head-view, first-order and TPDB extraction layers construct nodes and call graphs without marked pairs, without adequacy laws, and without proving semantic correspondence to the trace-kernel Step relation, which is explicitly left outside those modules.

Finite SCC, reachability and path layers apply only to finite decidable relations with non-variable-application left-hand sides where stated; bounded closure at Fintype.card steps is claimed only under finiteness, SCC witnesses and explicit edge paths are obtained only from supplied existence or TransGen proofs, and not all DP processors are formalized.
The internal replay record reuses the imported rank decrease from ko7ProjectionProblem and is explicitly not an external certificate replay.
Reach-gate test files only check elaboration, interfaces and axiom footprints and prove no new theory.

files.summary: This file bundles an exact subterm-criterion certificate for the KO7 dependency-pair problem with internal and external support kept distinct. It defines the certificate structure and its canonical KO7 instance at projection index 2, paper index 3, with rank dpRank. It proves internal strict descent, alignment of the existing TTT2 and CeTA replay to the same DPPair and projection index, their independent support for well-foundedness, and a closure marker.
files.conclusion: Internal Lean descent and external CeTA-backed replay independently support the same KO7 dependency-pair termination route.

files.summary: This file records that the extracted KO7 dependency-pair problem is a single predecessor drop on the recursor counter. It defines a simple linear counter-height base order and proves it orients the pair problem. It concludes there is no blanket negative theorem saying dependency pairs still fail whenever the base order is affine or polynomial.
files.conclusion: There is no blanket barrier against affine or polynomial dependency-pair base orders for the extracted KO7 problem.

files.summary: This module derives a binary edge relation from a caller-supplied finite call-graph presentation with node keys and successor-key sets. It builds the induced finite dependency-pair graph and reuses the finite SCC search surface. It repackages discovered SCCs as standard cycle witnesses and exposes contradiction theorems when a candidate measure fails to drop.
files.conclusion: Finite call-graph SCC witnesses yield direct contradictions against any non-dropping global orienter.

files.summary: This module removes one packaging layer by letting callers start from raw extracted node data in an array. The node type is generated as Fin nodes.size and the existing finite call-graph and SCC search surface is reexported. It provides node and successor-key projections, the canonical call-graph view, search, existence predicates, witnesses, and non-orientation theorems.
files.conclusion: Array-backed extracted node data directly yields the finite call-graph and SCC contradiction surface.

files.summary: This module removes the explicit rule-array layer for engines whose rules form a finite carrier type. It packages finite-carrier first-order, head-view, and extracted-data engines with typeclass views and adapters between them. The canonical first-order and head-view extraction surfaces are recovered by enumerating the carrier, including defined heads, nodes, call graphs, and SCC search.
files.conclusion: Finite rule carriers recover the full first-order, head-view, and extracted-data engine surfaces without explicit rule arrays.

files.summary: This module connects the finite SCC search layer to the dependency-pair fragment for a finite decidable pair relation. It reuses the finite SCC search surface and repackages a discovered SCC into the standard SCCCycle witness. It exposes the DP-style strict-drop obligation and contradiction theorems directly from the search result, without formalizing all DP processors.
files.conclusion: Finite SCC search directly yields the standard DP strict-drop obligation and its contrapositive.

files.summary: This module packages an internal first-order rewrite engine once as a single structure instead of passing rule arrays and extractors at each site. It reexports defined heads, extracted nodes, call graphs, SCC search, and contradiction theorems from the engine object. It adds typeclass views for finite and raw first-order engines with automatic conversion to the canonical FOTerm view.
files.conclusion: Packaged first-order engines directly expose defined heads, call graphs, and SCC contradictions without per-site rule arrays.

files.summary: This module computes defined heads, defined call-heads in right-hand sides, and an array-backed direct call graph from a finite first-order rule array. Each rule contributes at most one node and Finset storage collapses repeated heads, without constructing marked pairs or proving semantic correspondence. It adds a TPDB syntax bridge with root-head preservation and a concrete eight-rule KO7 fixture with counts and a recD successor.
files.conclusion: The KO7 eight-rule fixture extracts to eight nodes with defined heads integrate, merge, recD, eqW and a recD self-loop.

files.summary: Callers provide a finite array of rule records with left- and right-hand side maps into FOTerm. The module constructs one rule-level call-head record for each function-headed left side with its graph and SCC search surface. Pair-level extraction and source soundness need additional structure, and the file proves agreement with direct FORule extraction on canonical inputs.
files.conclusion: Rule-record frontends with FOTerm side maps directly yield call graphs and SCC non-orientation theorems.

files.summary: This module packages rank-based pair problems where every extracted pair strictly decreases a projection rank, and finite-path reasoning where a nonempty path forces strict decrease under any global orienter. It defines reverse relations with rank-based well-foundedness and a historically named SCCCycle holding a one-way TransGen path. It proves orientation propagates along paths and non-drop precludes global orientation.
files.conclusion: Rank decrease gives well-founded reverse pairs and any global orienter must drop along TransGen paths.

files.summary: An internal term carrier supplies a root-head observation and a finite Finset collection of call heads with collapse of repeats. The module constructs rule-level call-head records, a graph, and SCC wrappers from those observations, with adequacy laws outside the interface. It provides adapters from canonical and raw first-order views and engines built from the observations.
files.conclusion: Supplied root-head and call-head observations suffice to build rule graphs and SCC contradictions without adequacy laws.

files.summary: This module defines a hand-authored finite first-order system over KO7-shaped symbols with variables and constructor shorthands. It gives eight rules, a unit engine carrier, and a finite RuleId carrier with left- and right-hand sides plus instances across raw, head, carrier, and extracted views. It proves rule counts, defined heads, node counts, view agreement, and recD self-successors, with correspondence to the trace-kernel Step relation explicitly outside the module.
files.conclusion: The standalone eight-rule KO7-shaped model yields eight extracted nodes with a recD self-loop across all engine views.

files.summary: The pair relation contracts only a successor at the head of the counter, and RankedMachine supplies normalization laws for deterministic ranked relations. The file instantiates this for KO7 traces and for free recursor syntax with successor depth rank. It proves step characterizations, determinism, reachability, normality, idempotence, confluence, length and normal-form recurrences, and normalization certificates with length bounded by rank.
files.conclusion: KO7 and free recursor pairs are deterministic, confluent, and normalizing with explicit length and normal-form recurrences.

files.summary: This module connects the finite SCC search surface to the concrete TPDB and TTT2 export syntax via defined heads and defined call-heads in right-hand sides. It computes an array-backed rule-head call graph with one record per function-headed rule and Finset-collapsed repeats. It instantiates the construction on the exported KO7 full-step TRS with eight nodes, four defined heads, and a recD successor.
files.conclusion: The exported KO7 full-step TRS extracts to eight nodes with a recD self-loop.

files.summary: The file states the single dependency pair for the KO7 duplicating recursor rec_succ and defines a rank keeping only recursion-counter depth. It proves every pair step strictly decreases the rank and packages the data as a reusable projection problem. This yields well-foundedness of the reverse pair relation. It also embeds naturals as iterated delta counters inside the actual pair relation to transport well-foundedness to Nat.
files.conclusion: The reverse KO7 dependency-pair relation is well-founded and transports well-founded induction to the natural numbers via an explicit counter embedding.

files.summary: The file classifies all eight KO7 root steps and shows only R_rec_succ extracts a dependency pair, identified as DPPair.rec_succ. It proves soundness and completeness of extraction, pair-freedom of the other seven rules, strict rank decrease, well-foundedness, and nonvacuity. It shows a spurious control pair is neither a Step nor a DPPair.
files.conclusion: Extraction is sound and complete on the eight KO7 root rules, every extracted pair strictly decreases rank, and the DP relation is well-founded.

files.summary: The file specializes the generic TCAP over-approximation theorem to the KO7 singleton dependency-pair problem. It encodes the KO7 rules as a Nat-coded first-order TRS, defines real and estimated edges on one schema node, and proves every real edge is estimated with path and cycle transport. It adds concrete witnesses showing a real edge that is estimated and a pair with no estimated edge.
files.conclusion: The KO7 singleton DP problem inherits TCAP soundness, with both a covered real edge and an absent estimated edge witnessed.

files.summary: The file builds a self-contained first-order term model with substitution, rewriting, and TCAP capping. It proves the tcap invariant and step-closure lemmas culminating in the unconditional theorem that every real DP edge is an estimated edge. Its contrapositive gives a termination certificate that no estimated edge means no real chain step.
files.conclusion: TCAP estimation unconditionally over-approximates the real DP graph.

files.summary: The file defines one-step successor closure, bounded iteration and finite reachability at Fintype.card steps for a finite decidable relation. It proves soundness of bounded membership for reflexive-transitive closure and closure stabilization at the cardinality bound. It concludes that finite reachability coincides with reflexive-transitive closure and splits into equality or strict transitive closure.
files.conclusion: Bounded iteration to the cardinality of the finite type exactly characterizes reflexive-transitive reachability.

files.summary: The file defines distinct mutually reachable pairs and existence of a nontrivial SCC over a finite decidable graph. It builds the filtered finset of SCC pairs and a computable head search, proving the search succeeds exactly when an SCC exists. It packages a chosen witness pair and its two reachability directions via classical choice.
files.conclusion: Existence of a nontrivial SCC is equivalent to computable discovery of a concrete mutually reachable distinct pair.

files.summary: The file defines nonempty edge-indexed paths with per-edge certificates and single, prepend and append constructors. It proves by induction that every transitive-closure proof carries such a path. It extracts concrete paths and round-trip concatenations via classical choice.
files.conclusion: Every transitive-closure proof yields an explicit nonempty edge-indexed path.

files.summary: This file defines an internal dependency-pair replay record around ko7ProjectionProblem with fixed projection indices and counts. It proves index conventions, pair identification as DPPair, equality of Lean TPDB constants, defined-head sets, and recD self-successors across three encodings. It reuses the imported rank decrease to prove well-foundedness of the replay reverse relation and DPPairRev, explicitly not an external certificate replay.
files.conclusion: The internal replay record inherits well-foundedness from ko7ProjectionProblem, giving WellFounded DPPairRev.

files.summary: This file checks the exact subterm-criterion certificate surface with internal descent, external CeTA alignment and phase closure. It checks the canonical KO7 certificate, strict pair descent and reverse well-foundedness. It adds projection facts fixing paper index three, rank as dpRank and replay agreement.
files.conclusion: The canonical certificate has index two with rank dpRank, strict descent and CeTA-aligned well-foundedness.

files.summary: This reach gate audits DependencyPairs_Normalization without adding definitions. It checks projection-pair rank, free-pair well-foundedness, the rank versus length separation with counter encoding, and deterministic step and machine structure. It also checks normalization reachability, normality, idempotence, confluence certificates, and the parallel free-pair analogues.
files.conclusion: The normalization certificates and confluence infrastructure are reachable with baseline axioms.

files.summary: This file is a reach test for the estimated-DP-graph TCAP soundness module, checking pair nodes, replay and count lemmas, rule and edge definitions, transport and path and cycle lemmas, and positive and negative witnesses by #check. It provides four examples instantiating the self-loop estimated edge, the real-to-estimated over-approximation implication, a positive estimated edge, and absence of a negative estimated edge. It proves no new theory beyond these instantiations.
files.conclusion: The estimated graph over-approximates the real DP graph on the KO7 witnesses, including the self-loop and the positive and negative edge cases.

files.summary: This file forces elaboration of every public declaration of the estimated-DP-graph TCAP over-approximation module. It checks term, substitution, defined-symbol, TCAP, edge, rewrite, match and invariant notions, plus cap-invariance, step-closure, unconditional soundness and no-edge reflection lemmas. It prints axioms for the unconditional theorem and proves no new content.
files.conclusion: All estimated-DP-graph TCAP declarations elaborate and the unconditional over-approximation axiom footprint is exposed.
